title: Khwarezmid Empire
capsule: The Khwarezmid Empire, ruled by the Anushteginid (Khwarazmshah) dynasty, rose to become the largest Muslim polity in the eastern Islamic world by the early 13th century under Ala ad-Din Muhammad II (r. 1200–1220), who conquered Khorasan, Persia, and Transoxiana, deposing the Ghurid and Karakhanid dynasties. At its brief peak c. 1210–1218 the empire stretched from the Aral Sea to the Persian Gulf and from western Iran to the borders of India. Muhammad II's catastrophic decision to execute Mongol ambassadors and a trade caravan (1218) provoked Genghis Khan's systematic invasion: in 1219–1221 the great Silk Road cities of Otrar, Samarkand, Bukhara, Urgench, Merv, and Nishapur were sacked with massive casualties. The empire collapsed under the Mongol onslaught; Muhammad II died in flight on a Caspian island in 1220, and his son Jalal ad-Din Mingburnu fought a rearguard resistance until his death in 1231.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The empire's core in Transoxiana and Khorasan is documented by Persian administrative records (diwan registers) and geographical treatises, with post-conquest Mongol sources confirming city locations; peripheral control in western Persia and the Punjab approaches was transient and the boundaries for 1210–1219 are largely reconstructed from campaign narratives.
